card.statement:
One can give a slightly shorter proof of Proposition 4.4 as follows. Lemma 4.5 and the Verdier self-duality of the objects ${\mathbf{IC}}_{\lambda}$ show that these objects are parity complexes in the sense of [JMW, Definition 2.4] (for the constant pariversity). More precisely, ${\mathbf{IC}}_{\lambda}$ is even if $\dim(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda})$ is even, and odd if $\dim(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda})$ is odd. Now Proposition 4.4 is obvious if $\dim(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda})$ and $\dim(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\mu})$ do not have the same parity (because then ${\mathbf{IC}}_{\lambda}$ and ${\mathbf{IC}}_{\mu}$ live on different connected components of $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}$ ) and follows from [JMW, Corollary 2.8] if they do have the same parity.

4.4 Consequence on equivariance

Consider the category

$\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})$

of
${G_{\mathcal{O}}}$ -equivariant perverse sheaves on $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}$ ; see §A.1. (Here the stratification we consider is $\mathscr{S}$ .) We have a forgetful functor

$\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})\to{\mathord{\mathrm{P}_{\mathscr{S}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})}},$

which is fully faithful by construction.
As a consequence of Theorem 4.2, each object in
${\mathord{\mathrm{P}_{\mathscr{S}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})}}$ is isomorphic to a direct sum of the simple objects ${\mathbf{IC}}_{\lambda}$ , hence belongs to the essential image of this functor. We deduce the following.
card.label: Remark 4.7

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
